info.name: URL API Reference Add-Ons File API

params.name: removed
params.description: `true` to only include removed files in the response, `false` to include existing files. Defaults to `false`.

params.name: stored
params.description: `true` to only include files that were stored, `false` to include temporary ones. The default is unset: both stored and not stored files are returned.

params.name: limit
params.description: A preferred amount of files in a list for a single response. Defaults to 100, while the maximum is 1000.

params.name: ordering
params.description: Specifies the way files are sorted in a returned list. `datetime_uploaded` for ascending order, `-datetime_uploaded` for descending order.

params.name: from
params.description: A starting point for filtering the files. If provided, the value MUST adhere to the ISO 8601 Extended Date/Time Format (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`).

params.name: include
params.description: Include additional fields to the file object, such as: appdata.

items.docs: Getting a paginated list of files. If you need multiple results pages, use `previous`/`next` from the response to navigate back/forth.

Store a single file by UUID. When file is stored, it is available permanently. If not stored — it will only be available for 24 hours. If the parameter is omitted, it checks the `Auto file storing` setting of your Uploadcare project identified by the `public_key` provided in the `auth-param`.

Removes individual files. Returns file info.

Note: this operation removes the file from storage but doesn't invalidate CDN cache.

params.name: include
params.description: Include additional fields to the file object, such as: appdata.

items.docs: Get file information by its UUID (immutable).
Used to store multiple files in one go. Up to 100 files are supported per request. A JSON object holding your File list SHOULD be put into a request body.

Used to delete multiple files in one go. Up to 100 files are supported per request. A JSON object holding your File list SHOULD be put into a request body.

Note: this operation removes files from storage but doesn't invalidate CDN cache.

POST requests are used to copy original files or their modified versions to a default storage.

Source files MAY either be stored or just uploaded and MUST NOT be deleted.

Copying of large files is not supported at the moment. If the file CDN URL includes transformation operators, its size MUST NOT exceed 100 MB. If not, the size MUST NOT exceed 5 GB.

POST requests are used to copy original files or their modified versions to the S3 bucket.

Source files MAY either be stored or just uploaded and MUST NOT be deleted.

Copying of large files is not supported at the moment. File size MUST NOT exceed 5 GB.
